traditions/malankara-jacobite-syrian/nam: Jacobite Syrian Christian Church (Malankara Syriac Orthodox)
traditions/malankara-jacobite-syrian/sum: The part of the St Thomas Christians of Kerala that remains an integral, self-governing part of the Syriac Orthodox Church of Antioch under its Catholicos of India. It separated from the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in the disputes that began in 1912, reunited in 1958 and divided again from 1975. A 2017 Supreme Court of India judgement in favour of the Malankara Orthodox claim on parishes led to transfers of disputed churches.
traditions/malankara-jacobite-syrian/dis: Loyalty to the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Antioch
West Syriac liturgy (Qurbono) in Malayalam and Syriac
Long legal dispute with the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church
traditions/malankara-jacobite-syrian/pro: Scripture and the tradition of the Syriac Fathers and the first three ecumenical councils, with the Patriarch of Antioch as supreme head.
Salvation by grace through Christ received in faith, sacramental life, prayer and fasting.
Seven sacraments in the West Syriac rite; Holy Qurbono with the Liturgy of St James.
Resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed and intercession of the saints, especially Mary.
Catholicos of India (Maphrian) under the Patriarch of Antioch, with a local synod and the Malankara Jacobite Syrian Christian Association.
West Syriac liturgy in Malayalam and Syriac, with seven daily prayer hours.
Peshitta-tradition canon; in practice the broader Orthodox canon.
traditions/malankara-jacobite-syrian/sta: Active in Kerala and the diaspora; Catholicos Baselios Thomas I led it from 2002 until his death in 2024.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/name: Mar Thoma Syrian Church of Malabar
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/summary: A 'reformed Oriental' church of Kerala that keeps the West Syriac liturgical structure and episcopal order of the St Thomas Christians while adopting Reformation emphases: vernacular worship, Scripture's sole authority in doctrine, and the removal of prayers for the dead and invocation of saints. It grew from the reforms of Abraham Malpan (1836) and separated after an 1889 court verdict. Its Maramon Convention is one of the largest Christian gatherings in Asia.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/distinctives: Reformed West Syriac liturgy in Malayalam
Strong evangelistic and mission societies (Mar Thoma Evangelistic Association, 1888)
Communion relations with Anglican churches and the Church of South India
Member of the World Council of Churches
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/profile/auth: Holy Scripture as the supreme authority for faith, with the Nicene Creed and the Syriac liturgical heritage purified in its light.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/profile/salv: Salvation by grace through faith in Christ, expressed in personal conversion, holiness and witness.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/profile/sacr: Baptism and the Holy Qurbana as the chief sacraments, celebrated in a revised Syriac rite; confirmation, marriage and ordination retained as rites.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/profile/esch: Hope of Christ's return and eternal life; no prayers for the dead.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/profile/gove: Metropolitan and episcopal synod with an elected representative assembly (Prathinidhi Mandalam) of clergy and laity.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/profile/wors: Revised Liturgy of St James in Malayalam and other languages, with Bible study and evangelistic conventions.
traditions/mar-thoma-syrian/status: Active, with roughly a million members in India and the diaspora (church estimate).
traditions/armenian-catholicosate-cilici: Armenian Catholicosate of the Great House of Cilicia

One of the two catholicosates of the Armenian Apostolic Church. The supreme see had followed the Armenian kingdom to Cilicia; when a new catholicos was elected at Etchmiadzin in 1441, the line at Sis continued. After the genocide and the loss of Cilicia it was re-established at Antelias near Beirut (1930). During the Cold War it led much of the diaspora independently of Soviet-controlled Etchmiadzin; it shares the same faith and liturgy and recognises Etchmiadzin's primacy of honour.
Jurisdiction over Lebanon, Syria, Cyprus, Iran, the Gulf and part of the North American diaspora
Cold War-era rivalry and later cooperation with Etchmiadzin
Active ecumenical role in the Middle East Council of Churches and WCC
Scripture and the tradition of the first three ecumenical councils, the Armenian Fathers (e.g. Gregory the Illuminator, Nerses Shnorhali) and the Armenian liturgy.
Salvation by grace through the incarnate Christ, received in faith and the sacramental life.
Seven sacraments; unleavened bread and unmixed wine in the Eucharist (Badarak); infant communion.
Resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed; veneration of saints, including the genocide martyrs canonised in 2015.
Catholicos (Aram I since 1995) elected by a national ecclesiastical assembly of clergy and laity.
Armenian Divine Liturgy in Classical Armenian; Christmas and Theophany kept together on 6 January.
The Armenian Bible, broadly the Orthodox canon.
Active; leads several diaspora dioceses alongside Etchmiadzin's.
traditions/ancient-church-of-the-east/su: A branch of the Church of the East that separated from the Assyrian Church of the East in 1968, when opponents of Patriarch Eshai Shimun XXIII's adoption of the Gregorian calendar and of hereditary patriarchal succession consecrated Mar Thoma Darmo as patriarch in Baghdad. It shares the East Syriac faith, liturgy and heritage of the Assyrian church; dialogue on reunion has continued for decades.
traditions/ancient-church-of-the-east/di: Rejection of hereditary patriarchal succession (later also ended in the Assyrian church)
Reunion talks with the Assyrian Church of the East
traditions/ancient-church-of-the-east/pr: Scripture and the East Syriac Fathers (Theodore of Mopsuestia, Narsai, Babai the Great) and the synods of the Church of the East.
Salvation through Christ, the eternal Word who took a complete humanity, received through faith, baptism and the Holy Qurbana.
Sacraments ('Raze') including baptism, Eucharist, ordination and the Holy Leaven; the Anaphora of Addai and Mari.
Resurrection and judgement; prayer for the departed.
Catholicos-Patriarch (Mar Addai II, 1972–2022, then his successor) with a synod of metropolitans and bishops.
East Syriac liturgy in Syriac with Neo-Aramaic; Julian calendar.
traditions/ancient-church-of-the-east/st: Active, small, concentrated in Iraq and the diaspora.
traditions/chaldean-catholic/summary: The East Syriac church in communion with Rome, originating in the 1552–53 election and papal consecration of Yohannan Sulaqa and consolidated as a single 'Patriarchate of Babylon of the Chaldeans' in 1830. It is the largest church of Iraq; its patriarchate moved from Mosul to Baghdad in 1950. War, the 2014 Islamic State expulsions from Mosul and the Nineveh Plains, and emigration have greatly reduced its Iraqi presence and enlarged its diaspora (notably Detroit and San Diego).
traditions/chaldean-catholic/distinctive: East Syriac liturgy in communion with Rome
Seat in Baghdad; Cardinal Louis Raphaël I Sako patriarch from 2013
Large diaspora in the United States, Australia and Europe
traditions/chaldean-catholic/profile/aut: Scripture and Tradition with the magisterium of the Pope and bishops; the East Syriac Fathers and liturgy.
traditions/chaldean-catholic/profile/sal: Salvation by grace through Christ, received in faith and the sacraments, as in Catholic teaching.
traditions/chaldean-catholic/profile/sac: Seven sacraments in the East Syriac (Chaldean) rite; the Anaphora of Addai and Mari.
traditions/chaldean-catholic/profile/esc: Catholic eschatology: resurrection, judgement, heaven, purgatory and hell.
traditions/chaldean-catholic/profile/gov: Patriarch and synod as a church sui iuris under the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (1990).
traditions/chaldean-catholic/profile/wor: Chaldean liturgy in Syriac, Neo-Aramaic, Arabic and English.
traditions/maronite-catholic/summary: A Syriac-heritage church named after the hermit St Maron (d. c. 410) and the monastery founded in his memory; tradition names John Maron (d. 707) as its first patriarch. Maronites hold that they have never been out of communion with Rome; formal ties were reaffirmed during the Crusades (1182) and the Synod of Mount Lebanon (1736) codified their discipline. Centred on Mount Lebanon, the church has shaped modern Lebanon and has a large emigrant community, especially in Brazil and the Americas.
traditions/maronite-catholic/distinctive: The only Eastern Catholic church with no Orthodox counterpart
West Syriac (Antiochene) liturgy in Syriac and Arabic
Monastic and hermit tradition of the Qadisha valley
traditions/maronite-catholic/profile/aut: Scripture and Tradition interpreted by the magisterium of the Pope and bishops, together with the church's own patristic and liturgical heritage.
traditions/maronite-catholic/profile/sal: Salvation by grace through Christ, received in faith and the sacraments; Eastern Catholics often express this, like the Orthodox, as deification (theosis).
traditions/maronite-catholic/profile/sac: Seven sacraments; Maronite Qurbono with Syriac anaphoras; historic latinisations partly reversed since Vatican II.
traditions/maronite-catholic/profile/esc: Catholic teaching on resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell, with prayer for the departed; Eastern Catholics often describe purification after death in Eastern rather than Latin terms.
traditions/maronite-catholic/profile/gov: Patriarch of Antioch and All the East (Bechara Boutros al-Rahi since 2011) with the synod of bishops, governed as a church sui iuris under the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (1990), in full communion with the Bishop of Rome.
traditions/maronite-catholic/profile/wor: Maronite liturgy in Arabic and Syriac (and local languages abroad); Syriac chant.
traditions/melkite-greek-catholic/summar: The Byzantine-rite Arabic-speaking church in communion with Rome, formed when the 1724 patriarchal election in Antioch divided pro-Roman and pro-Constantinople parties. 'Melkite' (from Syriac malka, 'king') originally named the Chalcedonian 'imperial' Christians. At Vatican II, Patriarch Maximos IV Sayegh became a prominent defender of Eastern traditions and the dignity of the Eastern churches.
traditions/melkite-greek-catholic/distin: Byzantine liturgy in Arabic and Greek
Patriarch of Antioch, Alexandria and Jerusalem, resident in Damascus
Advocacy of Eastern ecclesiology within Catholicism (Maximos IV at Vatican II)
Close cultural kinship with the Antiochian Orthodox
traditions/melkite-greek-catholic/profil: Scripture and Tradition interpreted by the magisterium of the Pope and bishops, together with the church's own patristic and liturgical heritage.
Salvation by grace through Christ, received in faith and the sacraments; Eastern Catholics often express this, like the Orthodox, as deification (theosis).
Seven Mysteries in the Byzantine rite; chrismation and communion given to infants at baptism.
Catholic teaching on resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell, with prayer for the departed; Eastern Catholics often describe purification after death in Eastern rather than Latin terms.
Patriarch (Youssef Absi since 2017) with the Holy Synod, governed as a church sui iuris under the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (1990), in full communion with the Bishop of Rome.
Divine Liturgy of St John Chrysostom in Arabic, Greek and English; Byzantine chant.
traditions/ukrainian-greek-catholic/summ: The largest Eastern Catholic church, born of the Union of Brest (1596), by which bishops of the Kyivan metropolia accepted papal authority while keeping their Byzantine rite. Suppressed in the Russian Empire, it flourished in Habsburg Galicia, especially under Metropolitan Andrey Sheptytsky (1901–44). The Soviet-staged 'Synod of Lviv' (1946) abolished it, and it survived underground until 1989. Its Major Archbishop has resided in Kyiv since 2005.
traditions/ukrainian-greek-catholic/dist: Martyrdom and underground existence under Soviet rule (1946–1989)
Metropolitan Andrey Sheptytsky and the rescue of Jews during the Holocaust
Strong role in Ukrainian national and civic life
Seat in Kyiv; Major Archbishop Sviatoslav Shevchuk since 2011
traditions/ukrainian-greek-catholic/prof: Scripture and Tradition interpreted by the magisterium of the Pope and bishops, together with the church's own patristic and liturgical heritage.
Salvation by grace through Christ, received in faith and the sacraments; Eastern Catholics often express this, like the Orthodox, as deification (theosis).
Seven Mysteries in the Byzantine rite; infant communion restored in many eparchies.
Catholic teaching on resurrection, judgement, heaven and hell, with prayer for the departed; Eastern Catholics often describe purification after death in Eastern rather than Latin terms.
Major Archbishop of Kyiv-Halych with the Synod of Bishops, governed as a church sui iuris under the Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches (1990), in full communion with the Bishop of Rome.
Divine Liturgy in Ukrainian and Church Slavonic; Julian calendar historically, with a move to the Revised Julian calendar in 2023.
